newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares down in late IBIS as dollar falls.
newsitem.headline: German shares down in late IBIS as dollar falls.

text.p: German shares were pushed backwards and forwards on Thursday as they tracked movements in the dollar, but dealers said volumes were limited and the market was probably entering a consolidation phase.

The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day computerised trade in the DAX index of 30 top shares, slipped back to stand down 0.04 percent, or 1.02 points at 2,764.85 points, well-below its day's high as the dollar fell under the crucial 1.50 mark level.
Earlier, the DAX index had ended bourse trade largely flat, paring earlier losses as the dollar pushed above 1.50 marks. It closed down 2.16 points, a bare 0.08 percent, at 2,772.34.
Shares were largely unmoved after a widely expected decision by the German Bundesbank to keep interest rates unchanged.
Dealers said a recovery in the newly-floated shares of telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom had also been positive for the market during floor dealings.

Telekom ended bourse trade over one percent stronger, up 35 pfennigs at 32.15 pfennigs, with dealers saying profit-taking on the stock was petering out. But the stock was slightly lower in late IBIS dealings, down at 31.95 marks.

Shares in industrial group Daimler-Benz AG were firmer, gaining 27 pfennigs to 97.07 marks in bourse trade, after interest in the company following an interview with the company's chairman in a German business magazine.
Chairman Juergen Schrempp said he expected 1996 group sales growth of 10 to 11 percent.

Shares in electronics firm Siemens AG rose 38 pfennigs at 72.25 marks, after the company announced a rise in 1995/96 after-tax profit of 29 million marks, but later fell back to close nine pfennigs off at 71.78.

Steel manufacturer Thyssen was weaker than the rest of the market, slipping 5.50 marks to 278 marks, with dealers saying some players were worried ahead of the firm's publication of 1995/96 results on Friday.
The stock had recently been climbing on speculation that the firm would soon restructure.
